thread:
samir: seeing intermittent gRPC streaming stalls between gpu-pool nodes in pla-az1 during model-shard pulls. latency spikes then full hang ~8-12s before retry. logs show stalled chunk sends.
ops-bot: alert: grpc_stream_error_rate > 0.5% on cluster/gpu-pool at 13:42 UTC
maria: any recent infra changes this morning?
samir: we rolled SR-IOV VF driver + kernel bump on a subset of nodes (Mellanox driver update). suspect network/encap interaction.
kevin: can you grab a tcpdump of one of the hanging streams and an iperf between the two nodes? look for DF + oversized L3 len.
samir: iperf shows 9000->9000 ok. but when traffic goes through the pod-cni tunnel path some packets are ~8200 and never ack. tcpdump snippet from node egress: ```
14:12:33.123456 IP 10.10.5.21.54321 > 10.10.6.19.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:8271, ack 1, win 229, length 8270
IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, id 0, proto TCP (6), length 8288) 10.10.5.21 > 10.10.6.19
```
julia: that looks like large host-GSO segments leaving the VF with DF set and then being encapsulated (CNI) which reduces MTU -> fragments would be needed but DF blocks them -> blackhole at some switch. classic PMTU/GSO/encap interaction.
maria: our CNI MTU configured to 1440 for tunnel, but node host interfaces and SR-IOV VFs are left at 9000.
kevin: run `ethtool -k <if>` on the VF and the representing PF. if tx-gso is on but encapsulation happens below the offload layer you can end up with oversized L3 packets on wire. also check GRO/GSO per-VF.
samir: confirmed: ethtool -k eth0 shows: tx-gso: on, tx-tcp-segmentation: on on the VF, but gro off on the representor. driver/kernel mismatch.
julia: short-term mitigations: 1) enable TCP MTU probing: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` (helps find PMTU) 2) disable GSO/GRO on the VF interfaces (`ethtool -K <if> gso off gro off tso off`) 3) make CNI clamp MSS on TCP to avoid 9000-byte segments.
maria: which is safer to roll to all gpu nodes?
julia: enabling pmtu probing is lowest risk but only helps TCP; gRPC streaming uses HTTP/2 over TCP so it helps. disabling GSO on VF adds CPU overhead but stops oversized frames. prefer a targeted DaemonSet to flip offloads on affected SR-IOV nodes for now.
samir: deploying a test DaemonSet that runs `ethtool -K $IF gso off gro off tso off` on the 5 nodes in the affected pool, rolling now.
ops-bot: deploy started: ds/sriov-offload-disable 0->5 rolling update
kevin: after the first 2 nodes, grpc_stream_error_rate dropped to 0.03% for shards touching those nodes. looks promising.
maria: long-term fix? driver upgrade or CNI changes?
julia: long-term: (A) driver/kernel matrix alignment so VF offloads are consistent, (B) update CNI to do GSO-aware encapsulation or clamp MSS at the dataplane, (C) add node health checks for VF offload state.
samir: filed INF-1629 with logs, ethtool outputs, tcpdump, and iperf captures. attached the kernel/driver diff.
maria: add runbook steps for when stream stalls: check `ip -s link`, `ethtool -k`, `tcpdump -nn -s0 -A` for DF oversized packets, and `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing`.
julia: noted — will add to infra-runbook and make a short KB.
maria: :thumbsup:
kevin: good catch. rolling monitoring alert to watch for recurrence and add SR-IOV offload validation to node healthchecks.
samir: thanks — leaving the DS running for another 24h to collect metrics, will revert once driver patch lands.
